sourcedFrom: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PISTOL PPS M2 — Rev. a (2015)
cleanIntro: The PPS M2 is a single-stack striker-fired carry pistol, 81 mm barrel, 27 mm wide at the frame and 23 mm at the slide, with a loaded chamber VIEWPORT rather than an extractor indicator. Its field strip is the familiar Walther pattern — trigger press, take-down catch, slide off the front. What is specific to it is the magazine: three floorplate sizes change the grip length, and the medium and large ones carry a dust cover with its own removal sequence. The book publishes no striker or extractor disassembly, so the deep work here is the magazine and the sights.

steps.title: Confirm the pistol and the magazine you are holding
steps.action: Check the slide marking against the book: this is the PPS M2, in 9mm x 19 / 9mm x 21 or .40 S&W. Then look at the magazine's floorplate — small, medium extension or large extension — because that changes both the grip length and how the magazine comes apart.
steps.prose: The PPS M2 is not the original PPS and the two are not interchangeable at the bench: the M2 uses a push-button magazine release on the side of the grip where the original had a paddle at the trigger guard, and its magazine floorplates work differently. The frame length is deliberately variable — Walther sells three magazine lengths for each caliber and the pistol grows or shrinks with the magazine fitted, which is the whole design idea. In 9mm the three sizes give six, seven or eight rounds. Establish which you have before you strip anything.
steps.aside: The magazine tube and the number of witness holes are identical across the three sizes; only the floorplate changes the capacity. Do not judge capacity by the tube.
steps.quote: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PISTOL PPS M2
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PISTOL PPS M2 — Rev. a — Cover, PDF p.1

steps.title: Magazine out, and set it well aside
steps.action: Take a firing grip with the finger straight and outside the trigger guard, point the muzzle safely, press the magazine release on the side of the grip and draw the magazine out.
steps.prose: On a carry pistol the magazine is usually loaded and usually the one thing that gets put down within reach, which is exactly what must not happen here — this strip ends in a trigger press. A large-floorplate magazine has a finger extension that will catch on a holster mouth or a pocket seam on the way out, so pull it clear rather than letting it drop. Count what comes out through the witness holes. Then put it in another room, or at minimum off the bench.
steps.quote: You must follow this procedure every time the PPS leaves your hand, is cleaned, handed to you or another person, transported or stored.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PISTOL PPS M2 — Rev. a — 3.1 Inspecting the Pistol, printed p.10 (PDF p.10)

steps.title: Rack, lock open, and look through the viewport AND the chamber
steps.action: Grip the rear slide serrations, draw the slide fully rearward in one brisk stroke, and lock it open by letting it creep forward slightly while pressing up on the slide stop. Then look into the chamber and down through the magazine well.
steps.prose: The PPS M2 shows a loaded chamber through a viewport in the top of the ejection port — you look into the opening at the rear of the barrel hood and see the actual cartridge rim if a round is there. That is more direct than a painted extractor but it is still only an indicator, and Walther says light, cleanliness and discoloured ammunition all limit it. The surest method remains removing the magazine and locking the slide open, which is what you have just done. Do not obstruct the ejection port with your supporting hand while racking.
steps.quote: The PPS comes with a loaded chamber viewport (2.4.1 Fig. 1).
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PISTOL PPS M2 — Rev. a — 2.4.1 Loaded Chamber Viewport, printed p.8 (PDF p.8)
steps.warn: Do not rely upon the loaded chamber viewport to verify the presence or absence of a round. Check the chamber with the magazine out and the slide locked open.

steps.title: Both openings, before the finger moves
steps.action: With the slide locked open, verify the barrel chamber is empty by eye, then look down through the magazine well and confirm no ammunition remains anywhere in the pistol.
steps.prose: Two openings, two checks — this is the pair Walther requires immediately before the disassembly trigger press, and on a short single-stack the magazine well is small enough that a round sitting on the follower can hide from a casual glance. Get a light on it. Unload the magazine you set aside as well, pressing each cartridge forward out of the lips rather than trying to lever them up; on the M2's narrow lips that is how they get bent. A pistol with an empty chamber and a loaded magazine on the bench is still one movement away from being loaded.
steps.quote: inspect the chamber and magazine well (opening) to ensure that they are empty before pulling the trigger.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PISTOL PPS M2 — Rev. a — 4.1 Main Components, warning, printed p.15 (PDF p.15)

steps.title: Slide closed under control, then the trigger press
steps.action: Pull the slide slightly rearward off the stop and release it slowly so it runs forward into battery. Point the pistol in a safe direction and squeeze the trigger fully to the rear.
steps.prose: The PPS M2's take-down catch will not release with the striker cocked, so the press is a mechanical precondition and there is no way around it. It is also the point at which everything before it either paid off or did not — a live round left in the chamber discharges here, and the manual says so in those words. Ease the slide home rather than dropping it; there is no cartridge to strip and slamming it only hammers the extractor. The Quick Defense Trigger breaks at about 27 N with 7 mm of travel, identical every time.
steps.quote: Remove the magazine and unload the pistol. Lock the slide in the open position. Look into the chamber and down through the magazine well. Verify that no ammunition remains in the pistol.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PISTOL PPS M2 — Rev. a — 4.1.1 Field-Stripping Disassembly, printed p.15 (PDF p.15)
steps.warn: To complete disassembly you will be required to pull the trigger. If a live round is left in the chamber the pistol will discharge.

steps.title: Take-down catch down on both sides, slide off the front
steps.action: Grip the take-down catch from above, one finger each side, press it straight down, and keep it there while you run the slide forward off the frame.
steps.prose: Loading only one side cants the catch and it refuses — that is the moment people decide a PPS is seized when it is not. Coming from above keeps the hand behind the muzzle while the slide travels. The M2's slide is short and light and there is nothing to arrest it once the catch drops, so hold it as it comes off. Take the whole slide off in one movement rather than in stages.
steps.quote: Grip the take down catch from above on both sides and press downwards (4.1.1 Figure 1).
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PISTOL PPS M2 — Rev. a — 4.1.1 Field-Stripping Disassembly, printed p.15 (PDF p.15)

steps.title: Recoil assembly out against its spring, then the barrel
steps.action: Turn the slide over, lift the recoil guide rod assembly out from under the barrel while taking up the spring pressure, then lift the barrel out of the slide.
steps.prose: A carry pistol this small runs a stiff recoil spring for its size, and the polymer end sits in a recess under the barrel — pull rather than ease and it will jump. Take the pressure on a thumb and roll it out. The barrel then lifts free with nothing retaining it. That is the complete field strip: frame, slide, barrel, recoil guide rod assembly, and the manual's figure shows exactly those four so you can check nothing is still inside the slide.
steps.aside: It is normal for the recoil guide rod assembly to flex when it is reinstalled. Flex is not damage.
steps.quote: Remove the recoil guide rod assembly from below the barrel while taking up the spring pressure (4.1.1 Figure 2).
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PISTOL PPS M2 — Rev. a — 4.1.1 Field-Stripping Disassembly, printed p.15 (PDF p.15)

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Frame, slide, barrel, recoil guide rod assembly. That is the published PPS M2 field strip — the magazine and the sights are the only things the book takes further.
steps.prose: Compare the four against the main-components figure before opening a solvent bottle. Notice what is NOT here: the PPS M2 manual publishes no striker assembly removal and no extractor removal, unlike the PDP book. That is not an omission on your part; those procedures simply are not in this manual, so the slide gets cleaned from the outside. The deeper work Walther does publish is the magazine, which comes fully apart, and the front sight, which is changed with the pistol field stripped.
steps.quote: Move the slide forward, and remove it from the frame.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PISTOL PPS M2 — Rev. a — 4.1.1 Field-Stripping Disassembly, printed p.15 (PDF p.15)

deepSteps.title: Medium and large floorplates: the dust cover comes off FIRST
deepSteps.action: If your magazine has a medium or large floorplate, lift the dust cover before touching the floorplate catch. With a small screwdriver, gently lift the dust cover's left front end first, then its right front end, then its rear end, and take the cover off upwards.
deepSteps.prose: This step does not exist on a small-floorplate magazine, which is why the manual heads it by floorplate size — try to drift the catch on a medium or large magazine with the cover still on and the punch will not reach the hole. The order matters: left front, right front, then rear, working the cover loose in stages rather than levering one corner hard enough to crack it. Take your time with the screwdriver; the cover is polymer and the frame it clips to is what holds your grip extension in place. Lift it straight up once all three corners are free.
deepSteps.quote: For magazines with medium or large floorplate: Using e.g. a small screwdriver, first lift the Dust Cover’s left and second its right front end gently a little bit off the floorplate.
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PISTOL PPS M2 — Rev. a — 4.2.1 Magazine Disassembly, printed p.16 (PDF p.16)
deepSteps.warn: The magazine spring is under pressure. Control the floorplate catch and the spring while you remove the floorplate.

deepSteps.title: Punch the catch, and line the legs up if it is an extended plate
deepSteps.action: Depress the floorplate catch through the hole in the floorplate with a 4 mm punch. On a medium or large floorplate, align the legs of the floorplate parallel to the rear wall of the magazine tube as you do it. Then slide the floorplate forward off the tube while keeping the catch pressed.
deepSteps.prose: This is the specific limit that separates the three PPS M2 magazines: the extended floorplates have legs that wrap the tube, and unless those legs are parallel to the rear wall they bind on the tube and the plate simply will not slide, however hard the catch is pressed. A small floorplate has no legs and slides straight off. Keep a thumb over the plate throughout — the catch is the only thing holding a compressed spring, and it will leave at speed. Wear safety glasses; the manual asks for them by name on this operation.
deepSteps.quote: For magazines with medium or large floorplate: Align the legs of the floorplate parallel to the rear wall of the magazine tube
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PISTOL PPS M2 — Rev. a — 4.2.1 Magazine Disassembly, step 2, printed p.17 (PDF p.17)
deepSteps.warn: Wear safety glasses when disassembling or assembling the magazine.

deepSteps.title: Catch, spring and follower out of the tube
deepSteps.action: Take the floorplate catch and the spring carefully out through the bottom of the tube, then turn the tube right side up and remove the follower through the bottom.
deepSteps.prose: Everything leaves through the bottom, not the lips, and nothing needs force — if the follower will not pass, it has cocked in the tube and wants straightening rather than pushing. Note which way round the follower and the catch sat, because they go back in exactly the same orientation and the manual is explicit about that. This is the only way to get the carry lint and pocket grit out of a magazine that lives against the body, which is why a carry PPS M2 earns this more often than a range gun. Wipe the tube's inside dry rather than oiling it.
deepSteps.quote: Turn the tube right side up and remove the follower through the bottom of the tube.
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PISTOL PPS M2 — Rev. a — 4.2.1 Magazine Disassembly, step 5, printed p.17 (PDF p.17)

deepSteps.title: Front sight change: field strip first, and the screw thread must be dry
deepSteps.action: To change the front sight, field strip the pistol first. Remove the front sight screw with a screwdriver and press the front sight upwards and out of the slide. Assembly is the reverse.
deepSteps.prose: The PPS M2's elevation is adjusted by fitting a taller or shorter steel front sight, not by turning anything, so this is a maintenance operation rather than a tuning one. The sights are numbered and the higher the number the higher the sight, with each step moving the group about 5 cm at 25 m. Before the screw goes back, make sure both it and the thread inside the steel front sight are free of oil or grease, secure the thread with an industrial adhesive such as Loctite 648, and tighten only lightly — about 1 Nm. An oily thread will not hold the adhesive and the sight will walk off under recoil.
deepSteps.caution: Windage is drifted at the REAR sight with the rear sight adjustment tool. Do not remove the sleeve below the steel rear sight.
deepSteps.quote: Elevation adjustments are made by using front sights of varying height.
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PISTOL PPS M2 — Rev. a — 5.1 Sights, printed p.21 (PDF p.21)

deepSteps.title: Striker channel stays dry
deepSteps.action: Do not put any gun lubricant into the striker channel. Everywhere else: one drop on each slide guide and on the trigger bar, one drop on the safety plunger and one on the extractor plunger.
deepSteps.prose: The PPS M2 book does not publish a striker removal, so you cannot flush the channel out if you fill it — which makes the do-not-oil rule more binding here than on a pistol whose slide comes apart. Oil in there gathers powder and carbon into a paste that slows the striker and produces light strikes that look like an ammunition problem. Keep the barrel's film to its external surfaces and the ramp where the locking block cams it. Magazines get a film on their external metal surfaces only, never inside the tube.
deepSteps.caution: Do not over-lubricate. Excess lubricant attracts dirt, unburned powder and carbon residue, which interferes with function.
deepSteps.quote: Do not put any gun lubricant into the striker channel.
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PISTOL PPS M2 — Rev. a — 4.4 Lubrication, printed p.19 (PDF p.19)

cleaning.name: BARREL & CHAMBER
tasks: Brush from the CHAMBER end through until the bristles fully exit at the muzzle, then pull back until they fully exit the chamber end — never reverse the brush inside the bore
Powder-removing solvent and a brass bristle bore brush to lift lead and firing residue out of the 81 mm barrel
Wipe clean with patches or a swab, then a light film of gun lubricant on the barrel's external surfaces and on the ramp where the locking block cams the barrel
Before firing, wipe all preservative and excess oil out of the bore, chamber and exposed areas

cleaning.name: SLIDE, BREECH FACE & VIEWPORT
tasks: Small brush in solvent around the breech face, the chamber end of the barrel, the extractor and adjacent areas exposed to powder or primer residue
Clear the loaded chamber viewport at the rear of the barrel hood — fouling there is what makes the indicator useless
One drop of lubricant on the safety plunger and one on the extractor plunger
Striker channel DRY: no lubricant at any point

cleaning.name: FRAME & RAILS
tasks: Light brushing with solvent to lift residue off the frame
One drop of lubricant on each slide guide and one on the trigger bar
Light film of high quality gun lubricant on all external metal surfaces, then wipe clean
A carried PPS M2 earns this after handling, not only after firing — sweat reaches the frame rails

cleaning.name: MAGAZINES (SMALL / MEDIUM / LARGE)
tasks: Light film of gun lubricant on external metal surfaces only; wipe the tube interior dry
Medium and large magazines: dust cover off first, then align the floorplate legs parallel to the tube's rear wall before drifting the catch
Small magazines: no dust cover and no legs — the floorplate slides straight off once the catch is depressed
Inspect the feed lips and follower while the magazine is apart, and never use excessive force reassembling it
Safety glasses on for any magazine assembly or disassembly

cleaning.name: SOLVENT LIMITS
tasks: No ammonia-based or strong alkaline solvents on any Walther firearm
Avoid prolonged solvent immersion and prolonged ultrasonic cleaning; 50 °C is the ultrasonic ceiling
Cold climate: use a lubricant that will not congeal at low temperature

reassembly: Slide upside down, barrel in with the locking lugs oriented as the manual's figure shows.

Smaller black end of the recoil rod into the spring mounting at the front of the slide, then the large polymer end of the recoil spring into the lower barrel recess while taking up the spring pressure. Flex as it seats is normal.
Push the slide onto the frame from the front until the take-down catch engages, then release it and let it run fully forward into the locked position.
Magazine: follower, spring and floorplate catch back into the tube in exactly the orientation they came out. Never force them.

Slide the floorplate on until the catch's round projection engages its hole with an audible snap. On medium and large plates, hold the catch in and keep the floorplate legs parallel to the tube's rear wall as it goes on.
Medium and large plates: hold the dust cover with its pins downward, slide it over the tube starting from the magazine's rear wall, then press it gently and evenly down into the floorplate.
Dry-patch the bore and wipe the chamber before the pistol is loaded or carried.
fncheck: Magazine out and chamber confirmed empty: rack the slide and let it go — it must run fully into battery on its own with no drag. Lock it open on the slide stop and drop it with the thumb. Insert the empty magazine and pull down on the exposed floorplate; it must not move, and on a medium or large magazine the dust cover must be flush and captive. With the striker cocked the take-down catch must not depress; after a trigger press it should. Check the loaded chamber viewport is clear enough to see the barrel hood opening, and that the front sight screw is tight with its thread locked. Finally look at the rear sight: it should be tight in its slot with the sleeve below it undisturbed.
